claims.value: Beta cells make up about three quarters of each pancreatic islet and produce insulin, releasing it when blood glucose is high.
claims.quote: The beta cell produces the hormone insulin and makes up approximately 75 percent of each islet. Elevated blood glucose levels stimulate the release of insulin.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Beta cells detect excess glucose in the bloodstream and respond by releasing insulin into the blood.
claims.quote: specific endocrine cells in the pancreas detect excess glucose (the stimulus) in the bloodstream. These pancreatic beta cells respond to the increased level of blood glucose by releasing the hormone insulin into the bloodstream.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A calcium signal inside the beta cell triggers its release of insulin.
claims.quote: For example, in the β-cells of the pancreas, Ca2+ signaling leads to the release of insulin

figures.title: Islet of Langerhans (functional tissue unit)
figures.caption: Functional tissue unit: islet of Langerhans. An illustration of the smallest repeating unit of this tissue and the cell types in it. Alpha and beta cells of the pancreatic islets look alike in an ordinary stained section. Staining for the hormone each one makes tells them apart: glucagon in alpha cells, insulin in beta cells (Cell Ontology; HRA ASCT+B).
figures.alt: Illustration of the islet of Langerhans and its cell types.
